9772.t: From the Hebrew phrase עמנו אל (“God is with us”) from עם (“with”) with the 1st person plural ending ־נו, and אל (“God”).

9777.t: Feminine adjective, from Ἕλλην (Héllēn, “Greek”) + -ις (-ĭs, feminine suffix).

9779.t: Uncertain origin; usually linked to ἕρμα (hérma, “heap of stones”), itself of non-Indo-European substrate origin or from Proto-Indo-European *ser- (“to bind, put together”). Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin.

9763.t: Traditionally taken as a nominal formation from εἰλέω (eiléō, “to turn, wind”) (< *ϝελ-νέ-ω (*wel-né-ō)) with a suffix -ιξ (-ix), as seen also in ἧλιξ (hêlix, “of the same age”), χόλιξ (khólix, “guts”), δέλφιξ (délphix, “tripod”), further from…

9730.t: From ἐκτείνω (ekteínō, “I stretch out”) + -σις (-sĭs), from ἐκ (ek, “out”) + τείνω (teínō, “I stretch”).

9721.t: From Proto-Hellenic *édō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁édti, from *h₁ed- (“to eat”).

9765.t: Present stem from the e-grade of Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ- (“to follow”).

9758.t: From earlier ϝέπος (wépos), from Proto-Hellenic *wékʷos, from Proto-Indo-European *wékʷos, from *wekʷ- (“to speak”). Cognates include Sanskrit वचस् (vácas) and Avestan 𐬬𐬀𐬗𐬀𐬵- (vacah-).

9764.t: PIE word *sénos From Proto-Hellenic *hénos, from Proto-Indo-European *sénos (“old”). Cognates include Latin senex, Sanskrit सन (sana), Old Armenian հին (hin) and Gothic 𐍃𐌹𐌽𐌴𐌹𐌲𐍃 (sineigs).

9785.t: From Proto-Hellenic *auhṓs, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éwsōs (“dawn”), which was also personified as a goddess of dawn in Proto-Indo-European religion, corresponding to Ancient Greek goddess Ἠώς (Ēṓs).

9783.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wākʰā́, from Proto-Indo-European *sweh₂gʰ- (“to sound”). Cognate with Old English swōgan (“to resound”).

9739.t: From ἐμφαίνω (emphaínō, “I show, present”, from ἐν- (en-) + φαίνω (phaínō)) + -σις (-sĭs).

9780.t: From ἠθολόγος (ēthológos, “painting manners or character by mimic gestures”) from ἦθος (êthos, “character”) + λόγος (lógos, “account”).

9740.t: From ἐμφύω (emphŭ́ō, “implant”) + -τος (-tos), from ἐν- (en-, “in”) + φύω (phŭ́ō, “bring forth, produce”).

9732.t: From ἐλαύνω (elaúnō, “to strike”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

9741.t: Unknown. Schwyzer compared Sanskrit सनर (sanara), of uncertain meaning.

9760.t: No etymology. Being in the same semantic field of δοῦλος (doûlos), Beekes does not dismiss a Pre-Greek, in view, also, of the suffix -ιθ- (-īth-).

9748.t: Nominal formation in -σις (-sis) from ἐντυγχάνω (entunkhánō, “to meet with”).

9720.t: From rare ἐγκύω (enkŭ́ō, “to be pregnant”) + -ος (-os), from ἐν- (en-, “in-”) + κύω (kŭ́ō, “to conceive”).
